verdict.rationale: Cloudflare Realtime documents named DataChannels through its SFU API. Publishers choose ordering and retry settings per channel, subscribers can send opt-in reverse traffic, permissions can be granted via `PUT .../datachannels/update`, and an acknowledgment gate (`waitForAck`) is available. Data is controlled alongside audio and video in the same session, for chat, sensor updates, control events, and game input. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of DataChannel latency and behavior, and documented latency or throughput figures.

support.subject: As a developer, participants exchange low-latency arbitrary data in the session alongside audio and video, with a documented data API

citations.quote: Use the Realtime SFU API to control which endpoints publish or receive audio, video, and data.
Exchange chat, sensor updates, and control events between WebRTC endpoints.
Publishers can choose ordering and retry settings for each named DataChannel.
DataChannels now support opt-in reverse traffic from one subscriber back to the publisher on the same channel.
Stream a game from a Container to browsers, then send keyboard and pointer input back over DataChannels.
